cases.title: Spreadsheet Data Categorisation
cases.what: Give every row one label from a fixed list, and nothing outside the list.

shape.state: one row of raw text, on its own
shape.question: choice, over the labels you allow

cases.use: A sheet script posts each row to Jev together with the allowed categories, and writes the winning label into the target column. Because the categories are declared in the request, a label outside them cannot come back, which is what keeps a hand-checked column from growing invented values. Rows under your confidence threshold are left blank for a human.

code.label: one row in, one label out
code.src:
import json, urllib.request

CATS = {"groceries": "Food and groceries",
        "transport": "Travel and transport",
        "subs": "Subscriptions",
        "ignore": "Not a real expense"}

def label(row):
    body = {"model": "jev-latest", "state": row, "questions": {
        "category": {"type": "choice",
                     "instructions": "Which budget category does this bank line belong to?",
                     "criteria": CATS}}}
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/decisions",
        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + KEY,
                 "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    ans = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))["answers"]["category"]
    return ans["choice"] if ans["confidence"] > 0.6 else None

cases.use: Export the activity you already have (tenure, tier, seats, logins, support threads) and send one account per call with its fields named, because a bare list of ten accounts returns one answer ten times. code.label: named fields, one account per call
code.src:
BANDS = {"healthy": "Using it weekly and growing",
         "watch": "Usage slipping but still active",
         "risk": "Likely to cancel in the next quarter"}

def band(acct):
    state = ("Account %s. Plan %s. Seats %d of %d used. Logins last 30 days %d "
             "(previous 30 days %d). Open support threads: %s.") % (
        acct["name"], acct["plan"], acct["seats_used"], acct["seats"],
        acct["logins_30"], acct["logins_prev30"], acct["open_threads"])
    qs = {"band": {"type": "choice", "criteria": BANDS,
          "instructions": "Which retention band does %s belong in?" % acct["name"]}}
    return decide(state, qs)["band"]

cases.title: Output Verification and Model Calibration
cases.what: Measure how often the decision is right before you trust it with anything.

shape.state: one record from a labelled set, with the answer withheld
shape.question: the same question you will ask in production
shape.answer: the model’s pick, for you to compare against the human answer

cases.use: Build a validation set of a few dozen to a few hundred records a human has already labelled, run the loop without showing the answers, and count the matches. Misclassifications tell you where the labels are ambiguous, and the spread of probabilities tells you where the confidence cutoff belongs. The video’s own advice is fifty records or more before production; tune the cutoff on one set and hold some records back.

code.label: a labelled set, a match rate, a cutoff
code.src:
rows = json.load(open("labelled.json"))      # state + human label

hits, conf = 0, []
for r in rows:
    ans = decide(r["state"], LABEL_QUESTION)["category"]
    hits += ans["choice"] == r["label"]
    conf.append((ans["confidence"], ans["choice"] == r["label"]))

print("agreement %.1f%% of %d" % (100 * hits / len(rows), len(rows)))
for cut in (0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9):
    kept = [c for c in conf if c[0] >= cut]
    right = [c[1] for c in kept]
    print("cutoff %.1f keeps %d rows at %.1f%% correct"
          % (cut, len(kept), 100 * sum(right) / max(len(right), 1)))

cases.title: Inbox Pre Filtering for AI Agents
cases.what: Stop paying a frontier model to read spam.

shape.state: one message, sender and subject kept
shape.question: choice over the buckets you act on
shape.answer: one bucket per message; only the useful ones continue downstream

cases.use: Put the decision in front of the writing. Each message is bucketed as an actionable inquiry, a sponsorship, spam or phishing; spam and phishing are dropped, and only the messages that need a reply reach the model that drafts. In the video’s own run, 1,700 messages were sorted for eighteen cents. Keep the state to the fields the question needs, because the rest of the message is a distraction.

code.label: read the headers, drop the noise
code.src:
BUCKETS = {"inquiry": "A real person who needs a reply",
           "sponsor": "A commercial pitch, route to the deals file",
           "spam": "Bulk marketing, no reply",
           "phish": "Attempting to take credentials or money"}

for m in inbox(limit=500):
    state = "From %s. Subject %s. First 400 characters: %s" % (
        m["from"], m["subject"], m["body"][:400])
    ans = decide(state, {"bucket": {"type": "choice", "criteria": BUCKETS,
          "instructions": "Which bucket does this message belong in?"}})["bucket"]
    if ans["choice"] in ("inquiry", "sponsor"):
        hand_to_drafter(m, ans["choice"], ans["confidence"])

cases.use: Walk your own logs or process notes and ask, of each step, whether a typed decision would have done the job. The answer space is closed: either a decision fits, or the step needs writing, or it is a count and belongs in code. The same audit runs over a public catalogue of use cases when you are looking for ideas rather than for your own work.
